newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat remains mostly good to excellent.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat remains mostly good to excellent.

text.p: Kansas' winter wheat crop remained in mostly good to excellent condition during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop weather report.
Wheat condition was rated 22 percent excellent, 60 percent good, 16 percent and two percent poor. Last week it was rated 20 percent excellent, 65 percent good, 13 percent fair and two percent poor.
As of April 6, 45 percent of the wheat crop was jointing compared to three percent in 1996 and the average of 25 percent.
Wind damage to wheat was reported to be three percent moderate to severe, 11 percent light and 86 percent undamaged.
Insect and disease infestations remained minimal, with a few reports of armyworms, streak mosaic, greenbugs and leaf rust in isolated areas.
Seeding of oats progressed to 100 percent complete, ahead of 93 percent last year and the average of 82 percent.
Topsoil mositure condition improved and was rated 20 percent short to very short, 74 percent adequate and six surplus.
